I am 56, been working this little 2 mu plot of chili for many years now. Quzhou land is alright, sandy-loam, but you have to feed it well or the chili won't set good fruit. My wife and me handle most things ourselves, my son works in town so he sends a bit back but mostly we live off what this chili brings.

Last year I got around 2200 kg per mu of dry chili equivalent — fresh was higher but I sell some fresh, some dry. Price was decent, around 8-10 yuan per kg dry. So this little plot brought maybe 35,000-40,000 yuan gross for the two mu, minus inputs and the plastic film and labor for picking.

This year I will stick close to what worked. I buy hybrid seedlings from the dealer in town — the "Xianjiao" type with thick walls, neighbors all use it, the buyers from Henan like it. I won't try a new variety, too risky on only 2 mu, one bad year and we eat into savings.

For fertilizer I do it like this: before transplanting in late April I spread about 2 cart-loads of chicken manure I get from the chicken house down the road, plus one bag (40 kg) of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu as base. Then after the plants take and start flowering I top-dress with urea — about 20 kg per mu, split into two times. Then when fruits are setting heavily I give another shot of high-potassium compound, maybe 15 kg per mu, because chili needs potassium for the fruit to color properly and not crack. Adding it up: nitrogen comes to about 22-24 kg per mu, phosphorus around 8 kg, potassium around 14-15 kg. The dealer told me chili is "potassium-loving" and I saw it myself — the year I skimped on potassium the fruits were small.

Irrigation — I have my own well, so water is not the problem, just the electricity. I irrigate after transplanting to settle them in, then maybe every 10-12 days during fruit-setting and growing, so over the season probably 8 times. I use furrow irrigation, no drip on this small plot, drip costs too much for 2 mu.

Pesticides — chili is troublesome. Aphids come early, then thrips, then the anthracnose when it gets humid in July-August. I spray maybe 6-7 times across the season, alternating products so the bugs don't get used to it. The agro-shop owner advises me what to mix. I don't like spraying so much but if I lose fruit to disease the whole season is gone.

Tillage — I rotary till before transplanting, the small tractor service charges 50 yuan per mu, fine for me.

I lay plastic film on the ridges, helps with weeds and warmth, and I transplant the seedlings I bought through the holes.

Expected yield — if weather cooperates, no big hailstorm, I count on 2200 kg per mu dry equivalent again. If it's a good year maybe 2500.
